title: KV prefetch + streaming reassembly and external tool-call sanity check for newly onboarded quantized variants
creator: Ava Martinez
description: When we onboard quantized model variants (int8/int4) we must verify that the streaming output pipeline and external tool/function call integration behave identically to reference FP16 variants. This ticket covers a focused compatibility verification: ensure KV prefetch + chunked streaming reassembly does not break function/tool call boundaries, that prefix cache warming and backpressure preserve semantic ordering, and that version-pin routing will fallback cleanly to pinned compatible variants without losing in-flight tool-call handshakes.
acceptance_criteria: Automated conformance tests validate tool-call start/finish tokens are preserved across chunk boundaries for 99.9% of synthetic traces.
No regressions in latency tail (p99) larger than 15% vs FP16 baseline for canonical prompt sets under 95th percentile load.
When a pinned model variant is unavailable, the routing layer falls back to a compatible runtime variant and the tool-call handshake is retried without duplicate side effects.
Perf profiles for the new quantized variants are published to the model catalog with clear notes on streaming behavior and recommended kv_prefetch settings.
Conformance matrix entry added to onboarding docs and referenced in the model onboarding checklist.
test_plan: 1) Create synthetic tool-call benchmarks that produce multi-chunk streaming responses with embedded function-call markers. 2) Run against FP16 baseline and quantized variants across small/medium/large sequence lengths. 3) Validate token-level reassembly preserves tool-call start/end and argument payloads. 4) Inject backpressure and connection interruptions to verify idempotent retries and no double-invocation. 5) Publish perf profile artifacts and integrate into onboarding pipeline.
implementation_steps: Add a streaming conformance harness that emits randomized chunk splits and asserts tool-call token boundaries.
Enhance kv_prefetch tests to simulate cold vs warm prefixes and measure delta on p50/p95/p99 generation latency.
Instrument router to tag fallbacks and emit trace IDs for in-flight tool-calls so we can confirm handshake continuity.
Run a matrix of quantization settings (int8, int4) with and without kv cache enabled and capture diffs against baseline snapshots.
Publish a draft perf_profile JSON in the model catalog PR and wire the onboarding checklist to require perf_profile presence before GA.
Create a canary pipeline to run against two customer-like traffic shapes and monitor via console dashboards.
notes: Early spike showed that naive chunking can split JSON function args; need to ensure chunk-aware JSON reconstructor in stream client.
We should avoid changing streaming framing until conformance harness covers real tool-call encodings (tools may rely on newline/length framing).
Consider adding a streaming checksum header per chunk to detect reassembly corruption; out of scope for initial pass but noted for follow-up.
risks: If fallback routing replays function calls, external side effects could be duplicated; mitigation: idempotency keys and router-traced handshakes.
Quantization may change tokenization boundaries for rare tokens, which can alter JSON payload spacing; test vectors must include edge-case tokens.
Increasing kv_prefetch aggressively can increase GPU memory pressure on Dedicated pools; coordinate with infra owners.
decisions: Will require perf_profile entry as part of onboarding gating rather than optional documentation (agreed 2025-02-20).
Initial conformance run will target 3 representative open-source models plus one internal tuned variant (agreed 2025-02-21).
Fallback behavior: router will mark handshake as 'transient' and retry once with the fallback variant; further retries require operator review.
